A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MTL-KD research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, checklists, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MTL-KD benchmark results, teacher–student comparisons, RL-versus-KD experiments, and R3C ablations, including real-world results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons and an appendix experiment testing R3C segment lengths.

M1.justification: The teacher–student distillation procedure, KL loss, heavy-decoder architecture, masking, and R3C reconstruction procedure remain unchanged. Rewritten training explanations and the explicit wording of segment acceptance clarify existing operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six seen and ten unseen VRP variants, synthetic sizes from 100 to 1,000, CVRPLIB Set-X, and Solomon instances. The added segment-length study uses four existing tasks and introduces no new data domain or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RF-Transformer, RF-MTPOMO, RF-MVMoE, and CaDA comparisons on CVRP, VRPL, OVRP, and VRPTW across three sizes, substantially broadening the synthetic comparison set. Some RouteFinder variants already appeared in the large Set-X appendix, but their participation in Table 1 is new; CaDA was previously only cited.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes the reported student-training budget from 900 to 850 epochs; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The new appendix experiment compares random segment lengths with fixed lengths of 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 using 50 R3C iterations on 100-node instances.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests whether random reconstruction lengths outperform fixed lengths on four VRP variants. Figure 5 also revises the CVRP reordering curves within the existing component ablation. The teacher–student and RL-versus-KD analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both checklists report seeds fixed at 2025 and answer No to statistical-significance reporting. Neither version provides repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial comparator results, and new Table 5 reports segment-length outcomes: random sampling achieves CVRP cost 15.88 versus 15.91 for the best fixed length, while OVRP ties at 10.17. Figure 5 replaces the CVRP reordering traces, with final costs near 15.84 instead of 15.87. Existing benchmark-table values remain unchanged; Figure 4 changes are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, policy factorization, distillation and training losses, and architectural equations retain their mathematical content. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and none are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim label-free multi-task heavy-decoder training through distillation, improved inference through R3C, and generalization across tasks and scales. The explicit task counts added to the introduction already appeared in v1's abstract and do not expand the contribution claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C extends the diversity explanation specifically to random versus fixed reconstruction lengths, attributing the advantage to avoiding local optima. Its consistently-best wording requires qualification because OVRP ties at the reported precision. The heavy decoder's computational-cost limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Reported resource access changes substantially: v1 promises a later release and marks open access No, whereas v3 supplies a repository link in the abstract and identifies available code and trained models in Checklist 5. The PDFs establish this access disclosure, but cannot verify repository contents.

R1.justification: The introduction adds broader references, including NeuroLKH, neural deconstruction search, URS, and work on LLM-based optimization. The central positioning against light-decoder multi-task solvers and label-dependent heavy-decoder training remains. CaDA's publication entry does not constitute a newly introduced research work.

P1.justification: The introduction, student-training explanation, and related-work prose receive localized rewrites and terminology cleanup. v3 updates affiliations and contribution notes, adds acknowledgments, and inserts the sensitivity appendix while retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands and rearranges task blocks, and a segment-length table is added. Figures 4–5 receive font, label, legend, and axis adjustments; Figures 2 and 5 move. Existing appendix tables are largely retained with renumbering and layout shifts.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through additional Table 1 comparators and the focused R3C sensitivity study, while providing explicit code/model access information absent from v1. These are useful but bounded gains: the added comparisons cover four seen tasks, uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the new segment-length interpretation overlooks the displayed OVRP tie. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
